newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-SLUTSKAYA POISED TO RETAIN TITLE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-SLUTSKAYA POISED TO RETAIN TITLE.

text.p: Irina Slutskaya seemed poised to retain her European women's figure skating title after her two main rivals flopped in the short programme on Friday.

While Slutskaya easily won the programme, widespread predictions of a Russian sweep seemed fanciful in the extreme as teammates Maria Butyrskaya and Olga Markova plunged down the table. They were ninth and 10th respectively and both declined to comment on their performances.
Second and third places were held instead by two surprise contenders, Krisztina Czako of Hungary and Vanessa Gusmeroli of France.
Tall Czech veteran Lenka Kulovana was fourth and Yulia Lavrenchuk of Ukraine was fifth, one place ahead of five-times champion Surya Bonaly of France.

Slutskaya, who a year ago became the first Russian to win a women's international title, was delighted with her routine, which earned her marks of 5.7 and 5.8 from the judges out of the maximum of 6.0
She skated ninth in the field of 30 and her routine was highlighted by extending one arm in the air on two of her jumps, an effective manoeuvre that went down well.
"This was a perfect programme. I am quite happy with the marks and they could have been higher if I had skated later in the afternoon," she said.
Czako, 18, was a jumping phenomenon when she first appeared at 13, but subsequently lost her ability to land cleanly.
"When I was young I could jump good but nothing else. Then my coach told me 'OK, now you must learn to skate very beautiful'," she said.
"Now I have good choreography and today I could jump very well," she added, saying her programmes for this season had been devised by former Soviet Union men's European champion Igor Bobrin.
Gusmeroli, also 18, is only in her second year at senior level and placed eighth last year.
"I have worked very hard to improve on that," she said. She received the one first place vote that Slutskaya did not get.
Bonaly did a fine combination of two triple toe loops and an excellent double axel but muffed a triple salchow when she approached it incorrectly.
She declined comment but Didier Gailhaguet, her former coach and now French skating director, was scathing.

Gailhaguet, who was only persuanded last week that Bonaly was fit enough for the event after an achilles tendon injury last year, said: "I hoped she could at least perform well in the short programme. She was not on top of the ice, not balanced in her jumps. She did not skate the level we were expecting. It is disappointing from a five-times European champion."
Butyrskaya, who fell on her first jump, won the NKK Trophy in Japan in December as well as the Russian title in which Markova was second and Slutskaya third.
Markova skated to Ravel's "Bolero" but did not gain the required inspiration from Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean's magnificent performance to the same music at the 1984 Olympics.
Second two years ago, Markova made serious errors on two of her jumps.
